subject: general
question: In which of the following years were the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms introduced by the British Government in India to gradually establish self-governing institutions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms** were introduced in **1919** to provide limited self-governance to Indians. The reforms were named after the then Secretary of State for India, Edwin Montagu, and the Viceroy, Lord Chelmsford.
 
• The reforms were associated with the **Government of India Act, 1919**, which aimed to increase Indian participation in governance.
 
• The system of **diarchy** was introduced at the provincial level, dividing powers between elected Indian ministers and British officials. Certain subjects were reserved for British officials, while others were transferred to Indian ministers.
 
• The reforms provided for a bicameral legislature at the central level and expanded the electorate by introducing limited franchise based on property, education, and income qualifications.
 
• The reforms were criticized for being inadequate in meeting the demands for full self-governance and were seen as a tool to placate growing demands for independence.
 
• The **Montagu Declaration** of 1917 laid the foundation for these reforms, promising gradual development of Indian self-governing institutions.
 
• These reforms led to dissatisfaction among Indians, which ultimately contributed to the rise of the **Non-Cooperation Movement** led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 1919.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Government of India Act, 1919:**

 
 
• This act marked the beginning of constitutional reforms in British India.
 
• Introduced a **dual government system** or diarchy at the provincial level. Reserved subjects like police, justice, and irrigation were controlled by British officials, while transferred subjects like education, health, and agriculture were handled by Indian ministers.
 
 
 
• **Montagu Declaration of 1917:**
 
 
• This declaration was a promise of **self-governance** for Indians in the future, which led to the formulation of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
 
• It was meant to address the growing political unrest and demands for independence in India.
 
 
 
• **Criticisms of the Reforms:**
 
 
• The diarchy system was criticized for limiting real power for Indians, as the reserved subjects remained under British control.
 
• The franchise was very limited and excluded a majority of the Indian population.
 
• The reforms failed to address the demands for complete self-rule and were thus seen as a failed attempt to pacify Indians.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical context:**

 
 
• The reforms were introduced after World War I, during a time of increasing political awareness and activism among Indians.
 
• The **Home Rule Movement**, led by leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant, played a significant role in pressuring the British government for reforms.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Reforms:**
 
 
• The limited reforms led to widespread dissatisfaction and the initiation of the **Non-Cooperation Movement** under Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• These reforms laid the groundwork for subsequent acts like the **Government of India Act, 1935**, which further expanded self-governance but still fell short of granting independence.
 
• They are a significant milestone in India's constitutional development, showcasing the early stages of India's struggle for self-rule.
